summary.headline: Manba Finance Q1 FY27: NII up 36% YoY to INR42 crore, PAT up 36% to INR13 crore, AUM up 22% YoY to INR1,731 crore.
summary.overview: Manba Finance reported Q1 FY27 NII of INR42 crore (+36% YoY) and PAT of INR13 crore (+36% YoY), with AUM of INR1,731 crore (+22% YoY) and disbursements of INR226 crore (+37% YoY). Asset quality was stated as stable, with GNPA at 3.41% and NNPA at 2.52%, and ECL provisions of INR25 crore against an IRAC requirement of INR7.57 crore. Management reiterated 35-40% AUM growth guidance for FY27, entered South India via Namma Loan (Sreesastha) in Karnataka, and launched LAP for MSMEs and battery replacement finance for e-3W. Capital adequacy stood at 24.40%, with management planning to raise INR100 crore of preference capital by September or October.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited decline from ~29.81% in FY25; not disputed by management

financial_highlights.value: INR25 crore vs IRAC requirement INR7.57 crore
INR0.25 per share (face value INR10) for FY27

segments.name: Product mix (AUM)
segments.commentary: Two-wheeler 84.1%, top-up loans 5.1%, three-wheeler 3.1%, used vehicle loans 1.5%; management says over 95% of portfolio is secured. Management targets two-wheeler share falling to 75-77% by end FY27 and ~65% within three years.

segments.name: Asset quality (Stage-wise)
segments.commentary: Stage 1 assets INR1,619 crore (93.55%), Stage 2 INR53 crore (3.4%), gross Stage 3 INR59 crore (3.41%); Stage 2 reported lower QoQ.

segments.name: Namma Loan (Sreesastha) South entry
segments.commentary: Partnership operating as BC partner with 100% Manba funding; disbursements started in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu to follow within FY27; FY27 AUM target INR60-75 crore; breakeven expected in 9-12 months.

segments.name: MSME LAP
segments.commentary: Disbursement started in Q1 FY27; ticket size INR8-20 lakh; expected ~2-3% of AUM by FY27 end.

segments.name: Battery replacement finance (e-3W)
segments.commentary: Launched for existing e-3W customers, ticket size ~INR60,000, offered with OEM tie-ups; to be opened to wider market later.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth of 35-40% for FY27, reiterated by management.
ROA target around 3.5% for FY27, supported by higher-yield personal loan, top-up and used two-wheeler mix (~30% of further lending at higher IRR).
PAT growth expected to remain similar to historical performance; no explicit quarterly numbers given.
Raise INR100 crore of preference capital by September or latest October 2026.
No new northern states planned in FY27; focus on UP, MP, part of Rajasthan and South expansion.
Seasonality: AUM expected to jump in Q2 (festivals) and especially Q3 (Dussehra, Diwali).
capex_capacity: Operating in 130 locations across seven states (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, UP, and Karnataka just started); 1,700+ dealers; ~1,950 employees, 1,000+ in sales.
Proprietary tech (LOS, LMS, LAS) claimed at ~90% of tech and software; MSME LAP uses vendor-owned software (first such).
Planning considerably higher tech spend this year on personal loan software; management said overall tech spend as a share of expenses to stay in a similar range.
Wants to reach 15% market share in new states within four years; claims 12-14% share in mature states.
demand_pricing: Disbursement up 37% YoY to INR226 crore; management said disbursement growth of ~35% continuing in the current quarter.
Sanction speed: over 60% of loans sanctioned in one minute; 92% same-day sanctions.
Funding: cost of borrowing 10.86%, borrowing mix ~60% term loans, ~25% NCDs, balance PTC and cash credit.
Liquidity was ~INR350 crore at 31 March 2026; company raised INR100-150 crore in Q1 and held ~INR200 crore liquidity, which management linked to higher borrowing cost.

qa_highlights.question: Capital adequacy has fallen from ~29.81% to ~25-26%; will capital be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it anticipated the need and will raise INR100 crore by September or October, in the form of preference shares, to fund growth.

qa_highlights.question: What share of AUM will LAP/MSME reach by FY27 end, and what are ticket size and customer profile?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP expected at 2-3% of AUM by FY27 end; ticket size INR8-20 lakh targeting shop-owning businessmen.

qa_highlights.question: Which products will reduce two-wheeler dependence?
qa_highlights.answer: Personal loans, top-up loans (after vintage maturity), used two-wheeler loans, three-wheeler loans via TVS all-India tie-up, and small business loans (~INR6-7 crore disbursed monthly) and MSME LAP.

qa_highlights.question: Technology: proprietary vs outsourced and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: About 90% of tech is proprietary; personal loan software spend increasing this year; overall tech cost share expected to stay similar. No capex-to-revenue percentage given.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on profitability for coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give quarterly guidance but expects growth in line with history, AUM growth 35-40%, and similar PAT performance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowing decline QoQ and what is the cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing reduced because of ~INR350 crore liquidity at March-end; higher cost in the quarter came from carrying extra liquidity. No forward cost trajectory given beyond NIM commentary.

qa_highlights.question: Why was QoQ AUM growth only ~1%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonality: run-down in April-June with few festivals; expects a large jump in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Namma Loan AUM targets and breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 AUM target INR60-75 crore; breakeven in 9-12 months, possibly 6-7 months given early response; senior hire from TVS Motor and TVS Credit.

risks_watch: Capital adequacy has fallen from ~29.81% (FY25, per analyst) to 24.40%; INR100 crore preference capital raise targeted by September or latest October 2026 - watch for completion and dilution terms.
Borrowing cost of 10.86% rose QoQ as the company carried ~INR200 crore of surplus liquidity; watch whether cost falls as liquidity is deployed and whether NIM stays in the 13-14% range guided.

Two-wheeler concentration (84.1% of AUM) with target of 75-77% by FY27 end; delivery depends on personal loan, top-up, used two-wheeler, three-wheeler and small business loan ramp-up, which are early-stage.
AUM growth was only ~1% QoQ in Q1; management guides 35-40% FY27 growth and relies on a Q2/Q3 festive jump, so Q2 AUM print is a key checkpoint.

New South entry (Namma Loan/Sreesastha, Karnataka first, Tamil Nadu later) with FY27 AUM target INR60-75 crore and breakeven in 9-12 months; monitor early disbursement and credit performance in a new geography.
Asset quality: GNPA 3.41% and NNPA 2.52% with ECL provisions of INR25 crore; new MSME LAP and battery replacement products have no seasoning yet.
key_quotes: By September or latest by October, we will raise INR100 crores to for to manage our further growth and expansion.
So, we can't give, but we will definitely grow in the range of whatever we have performed historically.
So definitely September and most importantly third quarter will have a big jump in the AUM.
So, we are targeting around 3.5% ROA for the FY27.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth and profitability, reiterating 35-40% AUM growth and a ~3.5% ROA target for FY27. It was cautious on quarterly profit guidance, declining to give quarter-by-quarter numbers, and it was not specific on borrowing cost trajectory or capex as a percentage of revenue.

adds.what: Namma Loan (Sreesastha) South entry in Karnataka, FY27 AUM target INR60-75 crore via BC partner
MSME LAP product, disbursement started Q1 FY27, expected ~2-3% of AUM by FY27 end
Battery replacement finance for e-3W, launched for existing customers with OEM tie-ups

growth.why: Management reiterated 35-40% AUM growth guidance for FY27 with disbursements up 37% YoY and ~35% growth continuing in the current quarter, backed by new products and the Karnataka entry; Q1 AUM was only ~1% QoQ per the analyst, and the INR100 crore preference raise is a funding requirement rather than capacity.
